# Systems Run Workflow Active Source Eligibility Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `roadmap-drafting`
- Updated: `2026-07-29T04:05:14Z`

## Objective

Ensure Run & Test exposes and invokes release-backed workflows only while the owning workspace system remains active.

## Discovery

Release-backed workflow handlers currently query immutable releases without joining their owning System Builder lifecycle record. Archived records retain immutable releases by design, so those releases remain discoverable until application-owned workflow eligibility checks active ownership.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: The fix changes which workspace-owned immutable releases may cross the Run and Test interaction and execution boundary.
- Protected assets:
  - Workspace-owned system lifecycle authority
  - Exact immutable release identity
  - Deployment, data, and artifact-review action authority
- Trust boundaries:
  - System Builder lifecycle repository to application workflow discovery
  - Prepared release profile to explicit application invocation
  - Workspace-scoped host composition to API and IPC projections
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - An archived system release remains selectable and can be invoked.
  - A release whose owning system record is missing or belongs to another workspace is treated as active.
  - A system is archived after discovery but before preparation or invocation.
- Controls:
  - Application handlers derive eligibility from the authoritative workspace-owned system record.
  - Missing, archived, cross-workspace, and system-id-mismatched records fail closed.
  - Preparation and invocation re-check lifecycle eligibility instead of trusting a prior summary.
- Verification:
  - Focused discovery omission tests for archived and missing systems.
  - Focused stale lifecycle denial tests for preparation and invocation.
  - Desktop and server host-composition checks plus repository gates.
- Residual risks:
  - Previously installed deployments remain separate retained operational records and are not deleted by this visibility fix.

### Constraints

- Immutable releases and archived system history must remain retained and restorable.
- Lifecycle filtering belongs in application-owned eligibility, not renderer clients or persistence deletion.
- Discovery, preparation, and invocation must all reject missing, archived, cross-workspace, or mismatched owning systems.
- Reviewed execution-plan workflows remain governed by their separate plan lifecycle.

## High-level decisions

### Published system lifecycle model

How should Publish expose install, activation, execution, launch, stop, and uninstall without asking users to manage deployment internals?

Publish consolidation is user-directed. The lifecycle must preserve exact-release integrity, workspace isolation, truthful retained state, audit history, and secure runtime authority while presenting only actions that are valid for the current system state.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `retained-stateful-lifecycle`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intent-driven retained lifecycle (retained-stateful-lifecycle) | Retain one application-owned current deployment per release and host target. Install also activates. Stopped systems expose only state-valid Start, Activate or Deactivate, and Uninstall controls; running systems expose only Stop. Start automatically opens a qualified visual system and starts a nonvisual server without an Open System control. | yes | Provides the complete user outcome but requires coordinated contract, application, persistence, runtime-session, host, transport, shared-UI, release-rendering, and documentation changes; Preserves audit, rollback, exact-release integrity, workspace isolation, and truthful lifecycle state; Requires explicit handling for partial install-and-activate failure and for a runtime that starts successfully when automatic visual launch fails | Not installed exposes Install; Install performs install then activation without exposing a separate initial Activate step; Installed, active, and stopped exposes Start, Deactivate, and Uninstall; installed, inactive, and stopped exposes Activate and Uninstall; Running exposes Stop only; Stop returns the system to its prior installed activation state and eligible stopped controls; Uninstall is available for any stopped installed system and records an auditable retained transition instead of deleting history; Opaque deployment and run identifiers remain internal, duplicate install intents are idempotent, and the standalone Run & Test tab is removed; Qualified built-in visual systems open automatically from verified exact-release declarative content and typed runtime bindings; nonvisual servers start without an Open control; imported or authored execution remains unavailable without a qualified sandbox |
| Existing command facade (existing-command-facade) | Move the existing operations into Publish, automatically select identifiers, and keep the current install, activate, and zero-output run semantics. | no | Smaller and faster interface change; Avoids new persistence and runtime-session contracts; Does not launch the created system or provide meaningful Start and Stop behavior | The interface becomes simpler but continues to overstate runtime functionality; Uninstall and deactivate remain aliases or unsupported; A visual system still cannot open after Start |
| Ephemeral destructive lifecycle (ephemeral-destructive-lifecycle) | Launch a temporary interface directly from a release and delete deployment and session records when stopped or uninstalled. | no | Simple visible lifecycle with fewer retained records; Weakens audit, rollback, reconciliation, recovery, and operational history; Creates destructive deletion and cross-host consistency problems | Uninstall physically removes state and can orphan or erase historical evidence; Failure recovery cannot reliably distinguish stopped, lost, or deleted sessions; Conflicts with the repository's retained immutable release and audited deployment posture |

## Increment 1: Authoritative published-source catalog

- Id: `active-release-workflow-eligibility`
- Status: `pending`
- Dependencies: None

Make Run & Test expose supported workflows only for active published systems and label each exact release with the same recognizable system and build identity shown in Publish.

### Work packages

- **Shared published-source catalog** (`application-source-catalog`): Application-owned discovery joins active System Builder records, completed builds, and immutable releases into one workspace-scoped exact-source catalog with deterministic system and build labels.
- **Release workflow lifecycle enforcement** (`workflow-eligibility`): Records, review, and deployment handlers discover catalog sources and re-check active ownership during preparation and invocation so archived, deleted, mismatched, and stale sources fail closed.
- **Host and presentation parity** (`host-and-ui-parity`): Desktop and server hosts inject the same catalog, while the shared Run & Test UI presents system name, build version, publication context, and bounded technical release identity consistently.
- **Regression evidence and documentation** (`regression-docs`): Focused application, host, and UI tests prove Publish-to-Run & Test identity correlation and inactive-source exclusion, with canonical workflow documentation updated.

### Deliverables

- Shared application published-release source catalog
- Active lifecycle checks in every release-backed workflow handler
- Desktop and server host-composition parity
- Recognizable Run & Test source labels correlated to Publish system and build versions
- Archived, deleted, mismatched, stale-lifecycle, identity-correlation, and UI regression tests
- Updated workflow architecture, context guidance, and temporary report

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `published-source-correlated`: Every supported active published build is discoverable in Run & Test with a deterministic system-name and build-version label that maps to its exact immutable release. | local | not recorded |
| `inactive-releases-hidden`: Release-backed Run & Test profiles omit releases whose owning system is archived, deleted, cross-workspace, or mismatched while retaining their immutable history. | local | not recorded |
| `lifecycle-rechecked`: Preparation and invocation re-read active owning-system state and fail closed when lifecycle eligibility changes after discovery. | local | not recorded |
| `host-ui-parity`: Desktop and server compose the same authoritative source catalog, and shared UI tests prove published-source labels remain recognizable without renderer-owned authority. | local | not recorded |
| `security-lifecycle-reviewed`: Workspace isolation, exact release integrity, lifecycle authority, fail-closed denial, secure rollback, retained immutable history, and residual deployment-record risk are documented and evidenced. | local | not recorded |
| `repository-gates`: Focused catalog, handler, host, and UI tests pass before applicable documentation, architecture, build, and full repository gates run once for the completed increment. | local | not recorded |

### Verification

- Run focused source-catalog tests that correlate active Publish build summaries to exact Run & Test release sources and exclude archived, deleted, cross-workspace, and mismatched owners.
- Run focused records, review, and deployment handler tests for discovery plus post-discovery lifecycle denial.
- Run focused desktop/server composition and shared UI interaction tests for recognizable labels and capability-specific workflows.
- After the complete increment, run documentation, architecture, server and thin-client builds, and npm test once.

### Rollback

Remove the catalog-backed release workflow registrations so Run & Test fails closed while immutable releases, builds, system records, deployments, runs, and audit history remain unchanged.

### Excluded

- Deleting immutable releases, builds, revisions, deployments, runs, or audit records
- Changing archive and restore semantics in Manage
- Changing reviewed execution-plan workflow lifecycle
- Renderer-only filtering or renderer-owned release identity
- Changing release digests or republishing existing releases
